# The problem is that ^[a-z0-9] in regex matches ALL occurrences of non-alphanumeric chars
# When we have "C++ rocks!", it replaces the first occurrence, then the second occurrence of +

import re

# Using a different approach - find each single match position by using lookahead
def slugify(text):
    text = text.strip().lower()
    
    # Build result character by character
    i = 0
    while i < len(text):
        if text[i].isalnum():
            yield text[i]
            i += 1
        else:
            yield '-'
            i += 1
    
    return ''.join(yielded)

# Test cases
print("C++ rocks!", repr(slugify('C++ rocks!')))  # Should be 'c-rocks'
print("Hello World", repr(slugify('Hello World')))   # Should be 'hello-world'
print("  a   b  ", repr(slugify("  a   b  ")))        # Should be 'a-b'

# Verify all test cases from the test file
def test_slugify_simple():
    assert slugify("Hello World") == "hello-world"
test_slugify_simple()

def test_slugify_extra_spaces():
    assert slugify("  a   b  ") == "a-b"
test_slugify_extra_spaces()

def test_slugify_punctuation():
    assert slugify("C++ rocks!") == "c-rocks"
test_slugify_punctuation()

print("\nAll tests passed!")
